messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test case `testGetParsedOptionValue` sets up two options: one with a specified type (Number.class) and one without any type explicitly set (the "f" option). It then verifies that `getParsedOptionValue("f")` returns the string "foo". However, observe that:

- The method `CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue(String)` calls `getOptionValue(opt)` to get the string value, then calls `resolveOption(opt)` to get the Option object.
- If either option or the string value is null, it returns null.
- Otherwise, it calls `TypeHandler.createValue(res, option.getType())` to convert the option value string to the typed value.
- The method `Option.getType()` simply returns `type`, an instance variable which is never set by default in the constructors we inspected.
- The `TypeHandler.createValue(String, Class)` method checks the type class to convert the value. If none of the recognized classes match, it returns null.
- Since the default type is null (when not explicitly set), the call `TypeHandler.createValue` returns null for options without a type explicitly set.
- Hence, in the test, for option "f", which has no type set, `getParsedOptionValue("f")` returns null instead of the plain String "foo".

The bug is that the default type for an option is not String class but null, which causes the value to be parsed to null rather than left as raw string. The report notes that users expect the default type to be String if not explicitly set.

This could be fixed by:
- Setting the default type for an Option to String.class in its constructor.
- Or by `CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue` treating null type as String instead of passing null to `TypeHandler`.
- Alternatively, documenting this behavior clearly in the Javadoc.

The failing test and current bug report clearly align in indicating that lack of default Option.type causes `getParsedOptionValue` to return null for string arguments that don't have a type set explicitly.

The related recent issue about constructors is not directly relevant to this type default problem.

Hence the root cause is the missing default type initialization on Option leading to getParsedOptionValue returning null rather than the unconverted string value for options without an explicit type.

This diagnosis explains the failure observed in the test and the behavior described in the current bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
